subject.title: Provider key pools + bucket-aware cooldown/backoff on 429 (Gemini projects) to prevent retry storms

question: Should OpenClaw add a native generic provider/auth quota-bucket contract for Gemini project/account quota failures, and should that live in core auth/failover or in a provider/plugin-owned seam?
rationale: The remaining work is not just a missing branch; it chooses public config/state shape, fallback semantics, and ownership boundaries for provider credentials and quota groups.

options.title: Add generic quota-bucket contract
options.body: Introduce additive provider/auth bucket metadata and cooldown semantics while preserving current flat rotation defaults and documenting migration/status behavior.

options.title: Fold into broader provider-pool design
options.body: Keep this issue open but make #41135 the design owner, requiring that broader provider-profile routing explicitly covers Gemini project quota buckets before this closes.

options.title: Keep bucket logic outside core
options.body: Reject native core state and ask provider plugins or external operators to implement bucket grouping only through existing seams if no missing API is identified.

recommendation.title: Add generic quota-bucket contract
recommendation.body: Introduce additive provider/auth bucket metadata and cooldown semantics while preserving current flat rotation defaults and documenting migration/status behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Their history spans the generic key rotation helper, auth profile storage, and provider identity/config direction affected by this decision.
